CVE-2026-56392 is an integer overflow in unexpand buffer allocation that multiplies max_column_width by MB_LEN_MAX. That allocation path was introduced after coreutils 9.7 (multibyte expand/unexpand support; first present in 9.11). Debian trixie and this DHI package ship 9.7, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.
The DHI coreutils package backports the upstream uniq -w multibyte find_field() fix from commit d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371.

CVE-2026-8149 is a local availability issue in Bouncy Castle BC-FIPS 2.1.0-2.1.2 affecting specific CPU instruction sets (AVX, AVX-512f) on Linux x86_64. bc-fips 2.1.2 is bundled in the eclipse-temurin FIPS JRE as a transitive dependency required for FIPS 140-3 compliance (CMVP #4943). No upstream fix is available; the FIPS module certification requires bc-fips 2.1.0, and the JRE vendor has not released a patched version. The vulnerability requires local access and affects only the GCM cipher mode implementation. Cassandra FIPS variants inherit this dependency from the certified JRE and cannot independently upgrade bc-fips without breaking FIPS compliance. Tracking upstream eclipse-temurin for a certified update that resolves CVE-2026-8149 while maintaining CMVP #4943 certification.

CVE-2023-50570 involves a denial of service triggered by crafted IP address strings causing unbounded processing. Cassandra only processes IP addresses from trusted cluster configuration (cassandra.yaml seed nodes, gossip peers) and does not accept arbitrary IP address strings from untrusted user input.

CVE-2025-48924 involves uncontrolled recursion in ClassUtils.getClass() when processing specially crafted class name strings. commons-lang 2.4 is a transitive dependency in Cassandra and the vulnerable ClassUtils.getClass() method is not called by Cassandra application code. Cassandra does not pass untrusted class name strings to this method.

CVE-2012-5783 involves improper SSL certificate hostname validation in commons-httpclient. commons-httpclient 3.0.1 is a transitive dependency (via Hadoop) and is not used by Cassandra to make HTTPS connections. Cassandra uses Netty for inter-node TLS communication (ports 7000/7001) and the CQL native transport, neither of which relies on commons-httpclient.

CVE-2025-46392 involves uncontrolled resource consumption when parsing specially crafted configuration files. Cassandra configuration is sourced exclusively from operator-controlled files (cassandra.yaml) and is not derived from untrusted user input. An attacker would need existing write access to the configuration to trigger this path, at which point they already have administrative control of the node.
